_README: PROVISIONAL addendum skeleton for the Starbucks Contingency Addendum. Second skeleton,
appended after the letter skeleton, ALWAYS-EMITTING - no gating, no applies_when.
Its own index space, 0-based, independent of the letter manifest.
WHY PROVISIONAL: there is no addendum .docx. Built from Powder Springs, the less-edited of
the two sends. Douglasville is an edited copy and diverges in four places (see below), so
neither send is authoritative and Powder Springs is only the better reconstruction base.
Every paragraph here should be treated as provisional until the Starbucks-issued source
file is obtained.
DIVERGENCES between the two sends, all resolved in favour of Powder Springs:
1. Preamble (idx 2)    - present in Powder Springs, DELETED in Douglasville.
2. Recorded Documents  - PS: '...Document to Starbucks approval to be recorded on ___.'
DGV: '...Document subject to Starbucks approval.' (no date at all)
3. Third-party approv. - PS keeps the '[from _________]' bracket; DGV removes it.
4. Exhibit C           - PS uses an en dash, DGV a hyphen. (Outside this skeleton's range.)
Divergence 1 is the informative one: the preamble is a sample-language INSTRUCTION, so a
dealmaker deleting it is correct behaviour. Categorised `instruction`, never emitted.
HEADING QUESTION - needs checking against the loaded bodies before this is trusted:
In the LETTER template, section headings are FUSED into the clause paragraph
('PREMISES:\tApproximately _______ square feet of...'). In the ADDENDUM they are their own
paragraphs, separated from the body by a blank line. I have mapped heading and body to the
SAME canonical body (the pattern already used at letter paras 229-235, where five paragraphs
share landlord_signature_block). That is correct ONLY IF each loaded body_text contains its
heading. If the bodies exclude the headings, the four heading paragraphs need their own
treatment and I will re-key. Please check title_contingency/main's body_text and tell me.
SCOPE - deliberately ends at idx 16, and this is a judgement call worth your veto:
In both sends the addendum is followed by an exhibit block (Exhibit A Site Plan, B Signage,
C Parking, G Seven Pack + its bulleted contents, L Landscaping + two links, N Prohibited
Uses list, R Senior Documents, S Schedule of Critical Dates table) and then the Landlord
Workletter. NONE of that maps to a loaded canonical body, and the exhibits look like
ATTACHMENT machinery rather than body text - the schema already has attachment_requirements
for exactly this (used by contaminated sites). I have therefore scoped this skeleton to the
addendum proper. If you would rather the exhibit block be modelled as skeleton paragraphs,
say so and I will extend - but that is ~40 more paragraphs with no bodies behind them, which
under rule 1 means categorising every one of them with nothing to resolve against.
OTHER CONTINGENCY (idx 16) is a heading with NO body text in either send. Modelled as one
paragraph claiming other_contingency/main on the assumption the loaded body is the heading
plus an open per-deal fill. Confirm against the loaded body.
COMPANION CHANGE REQUIRED - do not land this alone:
The four addendum bodies must come OUT of _unjoined_bodies in the letter manifest in the
same change, or rule 4 fails on stale allowlist entries (which is exactly what it is for).
future_construction/main must come out too when it gets its letter-skeleton paragraph - it
rides with this work without being part of it, and is the easy one to forget. After both,
_unjoined_bodies should contain exactly sale_of_property/main and
early_termination/placeholder.
